## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to implement a small, practical bit rotation using only shifts and OR, a common low-level operation in compilers and algorithms.

## Key Concepts

- Bit shifts and masking
- Width awareness and undefined behavior avoidance
- Circular wrap-around without loops

## Code Example

```c
uint32_t rotateLeft32(uint32_t n, unsigned r) {
  unsigned s = r & 31;
  return (n << s) | (n >> (32 - s));
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you generalize to 64-bit n?
- What if language semantics define undefined shift amounts; how to guard?

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to derive a fast, branch-conscious solution for 128-bit integers; assesses comprehension of leading-zero concept and how to extend 64-bit intrinsics to 128 bits.

## Key Concepts

- Leading zeros counting in wide integers
- 64-bit intrinsics (clz) or portable fallbacks
- Branchless or minimal-branch reasoning for performance

## Code Example

```c
int countLeadingZeros128(uint128 x){
  if (x.hi != 0) return __builtin_clzll(x.hi);
  return 64 + __builtin_clzll(x.lo);
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you implement portable clz without compiler intrinsics?
- How would you extend to 256-bit widths with identical patterns?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tracks cross-word parity using SWAR folding without branches.

## Key Concepts
- Multi-word parity with bitwise folding
- SWAR technique to reduce 64-bit to 1 bit
- No loops or branches across 256 bits

## Code Example
```javascript
unsigned parity256(uint64_t a,uint64_t b,uint64_t c,uint64_t d){
  auto p64 = x => { x ^= x>>32; x ^= x>>16; x ^= x>>8; x ^= x>>4; x ^= x>>2; x ^= x>>1; return x & 1; };
  return p64(a) ^ p64(b) ^ p64(c) ^ p64(d);
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- Extend to 512-bit input; how to minimize temp storage?
- Compare branchless parity to a popcount-based approach on modern CPUs.
